name: grafana-api
description: Use when you need to make Grafana REST API calls (dashboards, data sources, ad-hoc SQL against the platform PostgreSQL, alerting endpoints) or work with Grafana dashboards stored in a repo's grafana/ folder — import, verify queries, read back state.
---

# Grafana REST API

Direct Grafana API access for the platform instance (`grafana-platform.medrocket.ru`,
Grafana **11.1.3** — a *custom build*: health reports commit `da5a557b…`, a couple of
endpoints/quirks differ from upstream, see below), classic PostgreSQL (and other)
data sources; other instances via env overrides. The skill is service-agnostic:
the token sees EVERY service's data sources — always pin yours (see Quick Reference).

## Quick Reference

- **Token:** `~/.tokens/grafana-platform.medrocket.ru/token.txt` (service-account `glsa_...`)
- **Base URL:** `https://grafana-platform.medrocket.ru/api`
- **Auth Header:** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- **API Docs:** `https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/developers/http_api/`
- **Raw helper:** `~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana.py`
- **SQL query:** `~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-query.py`
- **Dashboards:** `~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py`
- **Alerts:** `~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py`
- **Shared HTTP layer:** `scripts/grafana_common.py` (token/host/env, one client, the contract)
- **Data sources:** one per service on the platform instance (the DS name is the
  service name). Name ≠ uid (see gotchas) — resolve via `GET /api/datasources` and
  pin yours with `--ds` (or `GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS` for `grafana-query.py`).

All helpers are **Python, stdlib only** (urllib — no curl, no jq dependency),
share `grafana_common.py`, and share one output contract (below).

Other instances / defaults: `GRAFANA_HOST=<host> GRAFANA_SCHEME=http GRAFANA_TOKEN_FILE=<file>`
select a different host + token (the host also names the default token dir);
`GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS=<name-or-uid>` sets the default data source for `grafana-query.py`.

## Helper Scripts

### `grafana.py` — raw API call

```bash
# GET
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana.py GET "health"
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana.py GET "datasources" | jq -r '.[].uid + " " + .[].name'

# POST / PUT with JSON body
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana.py POST "dashboards/db" '{"dashboard":{...},"overwrite":true}'
```

Args: `METHOD PATH [query_string_or_json_body]` (query string for GET — appended
**verbatim**, you own the URL encoding; JSON body otherwise, also sent verbatim).

**Output contract (shared by ALL helper scripts):**

- `stdout` — the response body **only** (empty on 204). Pipe straight into `jq`,
  nothing to strip.
- `stderr` — one line per call: `HTTP <status> <METHOD> /api/<path>`.
- Exit codes: `0` = 2xx · `1` = other HTTP status (body still on stdout) ·
  `2` = usage/token · `3` = transport (DNS/TLS/timeout).

### `grafana-query.py` — run SQL, get a clean table

The workhorse for "what does this data look like / does this query work". Stdlib-only,
sends the SQL through the Grafana data source, substitutes `${__from...}`/`${__to...}`
and `$variable` occurrences, and prints columns (scalar queries → `name: value` lines).

```bash
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-query.py \
  "SELECT count(*) FROM my_table WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'"

# window + variables (raw substitution — see variable-quoting gotcha)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-query.py \
  "SELECT count(*) FROM my_table WHERE kind = 'direct'" \
  --from now-7d --to now

# pick a data source (name or uid — names are resolved via GET /api/datasources)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-query.py "SELECT 1" --ds my_service
```

Defaults: `--ds` = `$GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS` env, else the ONLY data source visible to
the token (with several visible the command refuses and lists candidates — never
guessing: a wrong DS means silently querying another service's database). Name or
uid (uid skips the lookup; the DS `type` is taken from the listing, so non-PostgreSQL
sources work too). Window `now-1d`..`now`, `--format table`.
Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` query/API error, `2` usage/token, `3` transport.

### `grafana-alerts.py` — alert rules (provisioning API, provenance header baked in)

`apply` dry-runs the rule's SQL via `/api/ds/query` **before** committing (catches syntax
errors without touching the rule). Updates and pause/unpause go through the **group PUT**
(`.../folder/{folderUid}/rule-groups/{group}`); fallback is delete+recreate.

```bash
# list all / by group / by folder  (uid | paused | group | title)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py list [--group my-group]

# full rule JSON — template for manual edits
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py show <uid>

# pause/unpause one or more (group PUT; recreate fallback)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py pause <uid>...
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py unpause <uid>...

# upsert a rule file (provisioning shape with "uid"): SQL dry-run, then group PUT if
# exists / collection POST if new
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py apply rule.json

# delete; --clean-group also removes the ruler group if it becomes empty
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py delete <uid> --clean-group
```

Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` API error, `2` usage, `3` transport.

### `grafana-dashboard.py` — get / import / duplicate / move / search

```bash
# compact overview: title, version, folder, panel count, all data-source refs, variables + allValue
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py get <uid>

# full JSON
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py get <uid> --json

# import (create/overwrite; --folder defaults to the CURRENT folder of the uid;
# refuses a stale file `version` — see gotchas — unless --force)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py import grafana/<name>.json \
  [--uid U] [--title T] [--folder F] [--force] [--no-verify]

# clone under a new uid (default title: "<src title> (<new-uid>)" — slug-safe)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py duplicate <uid> --new-uid clone-2

# move to a folder (uid or title, case-insensitive; root/general = General)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py move <uid> --folder <folder>

# search (matches title/tags — NOT uid; case-sensitive)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py search "some title word"
```

Behavior **enforced in code, not by convention** (each one cost real pain):

- Saves go through `POST /api/dashboards/db` (canonical upstream endpoint). The
  platform's `POST /api/dashboards/import` is a **non-upstream custom-build**
  addition; the script only falls back to it as a last-resort re-save.
- A stale `id` in the dashboard JSON is **always stripped** before saving
  (stale id + different uid ⇒ "Dashboard not found" on 11.1.3).
- `import` **refuses a stale base**: a file carrying a `version` for an existing
  uid must match the server's current version, or the save is declined and
  nothing is written (a save replaces the WHOLE dashboard, so a cached copy
  fetched before someone else's save would silently roll back their panels).
  `--force` overrides; the check is skipped for new uids and for `--uid`
  clone-style imports (there the file's version refers to the source).
- The target folder is **always pinned** in the save command: `--folder` wins,
  otherwise an existing uid keeps its current folder. A save without `folderId`
  silently moves the dashboard to General (see gotchas) — "just update the JSON"
  is never folder-neutral.
- Every save is **read-back-verified with backoff**: fresh dashboards carry a
  stale permission verdict (measured: 403 up to ~55s, readable by ~120s, clears
  on its own — no re-save needed). Delays 0/15/40/65s, then one last-resort
  re-save, then a loud failure with what to do. `--no-verify` skips this.
- `duplicate`'s default title embeds the **new** uid: the slug derives from the
  title, and a save whose slug already exists is **silently redirected** to the
  dashboard that owns the slug (see gotchas).

Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` API error, `2` usage, `3` transport.

## Verified endpoints

- `GET /api/health` — version + db status (start here to check the token).
- `GET /api/dashboards/uid/{uid}` — one dashboard (`{"dashboard", "meta", "uri"}`).
- **`POST /api/dashboards/db`** — the canonical SAVE (create/update/move): body
  `{"dashboard": {...}, "overwrite": true, "folderId": <id>}`; import bumps
  `version`. There is **no** `POST /dashboards/uid/{uid}` save route in 11.1.3.
  `folderId` is what actually moves a dashboard (0 = General); see the folderId
  gotcha before omitting it.
- `POST /api/dashboards/import` — **platform custom-build only** (NOT in upstream
  11.1.3 — this instance is a patched build); behaves like `/db`. The helpers
  use `/db` and only fall back to this as a last-resort re-save.
- `GET /api/search?query=...` (NOT `/api/dashboards/search` — that 404s)
- `GET /api/folders` — folder id/uid/title mapping (folders are usually per-service).
- `GET /api/datasources` — **only the data sources the token can see**; each has
  `id`, `uid`, `type`, `name`, `url`.
- `POST /api/ds/query` — ad-hoc query (see `grafana-query.py`); body
  `{"queries":[{"refId","datasource":{"type","uid"},"rawSql","rawQuery":true,"format",
  "intervalMs","maxDataPoints"}], "from":"now-1d","to":"now"}`.
- **Alerting on the platform instance runs on an external Cortex/Mimir ruler.**
  **The SA token has FULL CRUD via the provisioning API** (this is the write path —
  the ruler proxy itself refuses SA writes):
  - `GET /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules` — list all rules (200)
  - `GET /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/{uid}` — one rule (200)
  - **`POST /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules`** — CREATE (201). `PUT` with a NEW uid
    404s — create goes through the collection POST.
  - **Group PUT is the reliable UPDATE path:**
    `GET/PUT /api/v1/provisioning/folder/{folderUid}/rule-groups/{groupTitle}` — body
    `{"title", "folderUid", "interval": <SECONDS>, "rules": [full rule objects]}`.
    Replaces the whole group: fetch → mutate one rule → PUT. Honors
    `X-Disable-Provenance`. Use it for updates AND pause/unpause toggles.
  - **`PUT /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/{uid}`** — single-rule update; **BROKEN on
    the platform instance** (500 even on fresh verbatim bodies; devops saw
    `error="cannot find rule in the delta"` in Grafana logs — a server-side delta-sync
    bug, not a payload issue). It worked early in one session and then regressed; don't
    depend on it.
  - `DELETE /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/{uid}` — 204. **Leaves the (empty) ruler
    group behind** — remove it via the ruler DELETE below.
  - **Always send `X-Disable-Provenance: true` on provisioning writes.** Without it the
    rule gets `"provenance": "api"` and becomes **uneditable from the UI** (Grafana treats
    it as externally managed).
  - **Un-stamping an existing `provenance` is impossible via PUT (500)** — DELETE + POST
    the same rule back (same `uid`, no `id`) instead. (isPaused toggling has the same
    symptom on the single-PUT path, but works fine via the group PUT above.)
  - Provisioning shape is **camelCase**: `isPaused`, `noDataState`, `execErrState`, plus
    `orgID`, `folderUID` (namespace uid), `ruleGroup`, `notification_settings`, `record`.
    Best template: GET a real rule, mutate, PUT back. No `id` on create.
  - Ruler proxy (`/api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/...?subtype=cortex`) with the SA token:
    read (all groups / by folder / one group) and `DELETE .../{nsUid}/{group}` (202) only;
    `POST`/`PUT` there 404 for SA (a user-session cookie can POST a whole group — see
    write shape below). Use it for group-level listing, `interval`, and cleanup.
  - **No runtime alert-state API** (firing/pending/ok, history) — definitions only;
    state is UI-only or inside Cortex.
  - `GET /api/folders` for namespace uids (folders are usually per-service).
  - Ruler group reads: `GET .../api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/rules?subtype=cortex` — ALL groups
    (response is a dict: `{namespaceUID: [groups...]}`)
    - `GET .../api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/rules/{nsUid}?subtype=cortex` — groups in a folder
    (202)
  - `GET .../api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/rules/{nsUid}/{groupName}?subtype=cortex` — one group
  - `DELETE .../api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/rules/{nsUid}/{groupName}?subtype=cortex` — 202

### Alert-rule write shapes — there are TWO, don't mix them!

**Provisioning API** (SA token, preferred): camelCase flat object
(`isPaused`/`noDataState`/`execErrState`, `orgID`, `folderUID`, `ruleGroup`, `title`,
`condition`, `for`, `labels`, `annotations`, `notification_settings`, `record`, `data`).

**Ruler POST body** (user-session cookie only — whole group in one request), captured
from the browser; the group `name` goes in the BODY (no group in the path; PUT/POST with
a group in the path 404):

```json
{"name": "<group>", "interval": "5m", "rules": [{
  "for": "0s",                          // rule-level, NOT inside grafana_alert
  "annotations": {"summary": "... {{ $values.C.Value }} ..."},   // rule-level
  "labels": {...},                       // rule-level
  "grafana_alert": {
    "title": "...", "condition": "C",
    "no_data_state": "NoData",           // snake_case!
    "exec_err_state": "Error",           // snake_case; platform convention: "Error"
    "is_paused": true,                   // snake_case; omit uid on create
    "data": [ <A query>, <B reduce last over A>, <C threshold over B> ]
  }
}]}
```

The proven chain: A = PG query (`datasourceUid` = real uid, `model` with `rawSql`),
B = `type: "reduce"`, `expression: "A"`, `reducer: "last"`, C = `type: "threshold"` with
`conditions: [{evaluator: {params: [0], type: "gt"}, ...}]`, `datasourceUid: "__expr__"`.
A simpler `condition: "A"` (threshold in the query itself) also exists in the fleet.
Reference group to copy from: any existing `it-platform*` group
(`grafana-alerts.py list`); new-service groups should follow the same naming.

## Gotchas (learned the hard way)

- **Data source uid ≠ name** (on the platform instance the DS name is the service
  name, and the uid is an unrelated random string). Dashboards/panels reference the
  **uid**; a wrong one gives
  `"Data source not found"` on every panel while the dashboard JSON looks fine.
  When porting a dashboard between Grafana instances, diff the uid first.
- **`/api/ds/query` frames are column-oriented:** `frame.data.values[i]` is the list of
  values for field `i` (not rows). Single-row queries: `values[i][0]`.
- **PG variable interpolation:** option values from a variable query are substituted
  **quoted** (`$var` → `'option-value'`), but the variable's **allValue is substituted
  raw**. The working pattern: unquoted `$var` in SQL
  (`AND ($var = 'All' OR column = $var)`) + a **quoted** allValue
  (`"allValue": "'All'"`). Both quoting it yourself *and* an unquoted allValue break:
  `''option-value''` (syntax error) or `All = 'All'` (bare identifier).
- **Alert rule queries cannot use dashboard variables** and have no dashboard time
  range — write self-contained SQL with `now() - interval '...'`.
- **Time columns:** in `time_series` format the classic PG source converts a `timestamptz`
  column to a time field; in `table` format that conversion is version-dependent
  (12.4.3 converts, 11.1.3 hands back epoch-ms numbers → `1.79 Tri` on the axis).
  Environment-proof pattern for a matrix pivot on time: query
  `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM date_trunc('hour', created_at)) * 1000 AS "time"` (plain number)
  + transforms `groupingToMatrix` (row=time, column=<series>, value=<metric>) then
  `convertFieldType` on the pivot's time column
  (`"options":{"conversions":[{"targetField":"time\\<columnField>","destinationType":"time"}]}`
  — numeric input is read as epoch **milliseconds**).
- **Duration axis units (11.1.3):** the hh:mm:ss duration unit is **`dthms`**
  ("duration (hh:mm:ss)", Time category; zero-padded, hours unbounded, input in
  seconds). There is NO `hms` id — an unknown unit id renders as `NNN hms`
  (raw value + id). Siblings: `dtdurations` (s), `dtdurationms` (ms),
  `dtdhms` (d hh:mm:ss). Registry: `packages/grafana-data/src/valueFormats/categories.ts`.
- **The PG source has no "series column"** option (that's the MySQL source).
  Per-category series come from the matrix transform above.
- **Bar chart label crowding:** option `xTickLabelSpacing`
  (UI: "X-axis labels minimum spacing"; None=0 / Small=100 / Medium=200 / Large=300)
  in each barchart panel's `options` — time ticks on hourly buckets overlap without it.
- **Barchart's time X-axis is DATA-DRIVEN** (min/max of the returned rows), while
  **timeseries' time axis spans the panel's time range**. Same data, different
  axis width: a barchart whose data starts late fills the whole panel and looks
  like it shows "more data" than the timeseries next to it. Barchart has no
  time-axis min/max option. To pin a barchart's axis to the dashboard's time
  filter, return EVERY hour of the filter range from SQL: `generate_series(
  date_trunc('hour', $__from), date_trunc('hour', $__to), interval '1 hour')`
  LEFT JOINed to the aggregation, values `COALESCE(x, 0)`.
- **Importing a dashboard JSON with a STALE `id` + a DIFFERENT `uid` fails** with
  `"Dashboard not found"` (the pre-save validation chases the id). When cloning a
  dashboard under a new uid, drop `id` from the JSON first —
  `grafana-dashboard.py import/duplicate` do this automatically. (Same uid + same
  id is fine — that's a normal overwrite.)
- **Freshly created dashboards 403 on read for a while — a STALE PERMISSION
  VERDICT**, measured on the platform instance: 403 up to ~55s after create,
  readable by ~70–120s, and it clears **on its own, with no write**. Don't
  "fix" it by re-saving (bumps `version` for nothing, and the re-save can
  itself be 403'd) — back off and re-read. `grafana-dashboard.py` does exactly
  this (delays 0/15/40/65s, then a last-resort re-save via
  `/dashboards/import`, then a loud failure).
- **A save without `folderId` in the command relocates the dashboard to
  General.** `GetDashboardModel` overwrites the stored `folderId` with the
  command's value unconditionally (11.1.3, `pkg/services/dashboards/models.go`) —
  "update the JSON" is not folder-neutral. `grafana-dashboard.py` always pins
  the folder explicitly.
- **Slug collision = silent redirect.** The slug derives from the title. Saving
  a NEW uid whose slug already exists is silently redirected to the dashboard
  that OWNS the slug: the response's `uid` is the other dashboard's and the
  requested uid is never created (measured). Pick titles whose slug is free —
  the `duplicate` default `<src title> (<new-uid>)` is deterministic and unique.
- **`/api/search?query=` matches title and tags only — NOT uid — and is
  case-sensitive** (a Russian title needs the real case; URL-encode the
  query). To look a dashboard up by uid, use `GET /dashboards/uid/{uid}` or
  `grafana-dashboard.py get`.
- **`POST /rules/{ns}` and `PUT .../groups` replace the WHOLE group** — own the whole
  object, don't assume merge. (The `/api/v1/policies` full-tree-replace caveat applies
  where the standard API exists.)
- **Read vs write shape mismatch on the ruler:** reads give camelCase
  (`noDataState`, `isPaused`) + `expr`/`id`/`orgId`; writes want snake_case
  (`no_data_state`, `is_paused`), rule-level `for`/`annotations`/`labels`, and no `expr`.
  Copy a real group from the UI capture, not from the read API.
- **`count(*)` + `percentile_cont`:** `percentile_cont` over an empty set returns NULL
  (row still exists) — alert rules want `noDataState: NoData` to stay quiet when there
  is simply no traffic.

## Error Handling

- **401/403:** token missing/insufficient scope — check the file exists; the platform
  token is a service-account token with org-level access.
- **404 on `/api/datasources/uid/{uid}`:** the data source exists but is outside the
  token's view, or the uid is wrong — list `GET /api/datasources` and match by name.
- **`"Data source not found"` from `/api/ds/query`:** wrong uid in the query body.
- **`"Bad request"` / SQL errors from `/api/ds/query`:** the error text is in
  `results.A.error` — read it, don't guess.

import random
import string

from django.contrib.postgres.indexes import BrinIndex
from django.core.validators import MinValueValidator, MaxValueValidator
from django.db import models, IntegrityError
from django.db.models import F, Index

from users.models import User
from utils.models import AutoDateMixin
from service_template.feature_flags import is_feature_enabled

CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits  # Символы 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789'


class ShortLink(AutoDateMixin, models.Model):
    """
    Модель: Короткой ссылки
    """

    link = models.CharField('Изначальная ссылка', max_length=500)
    short_link = models.CharField('Короткая ссылка', max_length=8, unique=True)
    short_link_length = models.PositiveSmallIntegerField(
        'Количество символов короткой ссылки',
        default=8,
        validators=[MinValueValidator(5), MaxValueValidator(8)],
    )
    short_link_domain = models.CharField('Домен короткой ссылки', max_length=30, default='pd.tc')
    redirect_count = models.IntegerField('Количество переходов', default=0)
    comment = models.TextField('Комментарий', blank=True)
    active_until = models.DateTimeField('Активна до', null=True, blank=True)
    created_by = models.ForeignKey(
        User,
        blank=True,
        null=True,
        on_delete=models.SET_NULL,
        verbose_name='Кем создано',
    )

    class Meta:
        verbose_name = 'Короткая ссылка'
        verbose_name_plural = 'Короткие ссылки'
        ordering = ('-id',)
        indexes = [
            BrinIndex(fields=['dt_created'], name='shortlink_dt_created_index'),
            Index(fields=['short_link_domain'], name='shortlink_sld_index'),
            Index(fields=['active_until'], name='shortlink_au_index'),
        ]

    def __str__(self):
        return self.get_name()

    def save(self, *args, **kargs):
        if not self.pk:
            if is_feature_enabled('use_constraint_in_save'):
                dept = 0
                while True:
                    try:
                        self.short_link = self.get_random_string(self.short_link_length)
                        super().save(*args, **kargs)
                    except IntegrityError:
                        if dept > 5:
                            raise

                        dept += 1
                    else:
                        break
            else:
                # При создании генерируется короткая ссылка
                self.gen_short_link()
                super().save(*args, **kargs)

    def get_name(self) -> str:
        return self.short_link

    def get_full_short_link(self):
        return f'https://{self.short_link_domain}/{self.short_link}'

    get_full_short_link.short_description = 'Полная ссылка'

    def add_redirect_count(self):
        return ShortLink.objects.filter(pk=self.pk).update(redirect_count=F('redirect_count') + 1)

    @staticmethod
    def get_random_string(length):
        return ''.join(random.choice(CHARS) for i in range(length))

    @staticmethod
    def get_domain(request):
        return request.META.get('HTTP_HOST', 'pd.tc')

    def gen_short_link(self) -> None:
        """
        Генерация короткой ссылки

        * random.choice - был выбран потому что это самый быстрый вариант с меньшей вероятность коллизии
        для уникального кода с 6 символами
        """
        dept = 0
        while True:
            new_short_link = self.get_random_string(self.short_link_length)
            if not ShortLink.objects.filter(short_link=new_short_link).exists():
                self.short_link = new_short_link
                break
            # Можно свой Exception вернуть и во вью перехватить для красивого ответа вместо 500. Если потребуется
            assert dept < 5, 'Слишком много попыток сгенерировать ссылку'
            dept += 1

def detect_bot(user_agent: str) -> bool:
    """Определяет, является ли этот запрос от бота по его User-Agent."""
    info = DeviceDetector(user_agent, skip_device_detection=True).parse()
    if info.is_bot():

    if user_agent.startswith('WhatsApp/'):

from rest_framework.exceptions import ValidationError
from rest_framework import serializers

from short_links.models import ShortLink


class ShortLinkSerializer(serializers.ModelSerializer):
    short_link = serializers.CharField(source='get_full_short_link', read_only=True)
    comment = serializers.CharField(required=False)

    class Meta:
        model = ShortLink
        fields = ('link', 'short_link', 'short_link_length', 'active_until', 'comment')
        extra_kwargs = {
            'short_link_length': {'write_only': True},
            'active_until': {'write_only': True},
        }

    def validate_link(self, link):  # pylint: disable=no-self-use
        """
        - проверка домена
        """
        _, netloc, _, _, _, _ = urlparse(link)
        domain, _ = split_domain_port(netloc)
        if not settings.SKIP_DOMAIN_CHECK and domain not in settings.ALLOWED_LINK_DOMAINS:
            raise ValidationError(
                f'domain error, {domain} is not allowed, only {settings.ALLOWED_LINK_DOMAINS} allowed',
            )
        return link

    def create(self, validated_data):
        validated_data['short_link_domain'] = ShortLink.get_domain(self.context['request'])
        # Если в БД уже есть эта ссылка. То не генерируем новую, а берём старую
        short_link = None

        active_until = validated_data.get('active_until', None)
        # Если у создаваемой ссылки не ограничения по времени, то решили,
        # что нужно отдавать существующую, если она есть
        if not active_until:
            # Почему-то БД запрос такого вида выполняет очень медленно,
            # но тот же запрос без ORDER BY ... LIMIT 1 - быстро
            short_links = sorted(
                ShortLink.objects.filter(
                    link=validated_data['link'],
                    short_link_domain=validated_data['short_link_domain'],
                    active_until__isnull=True,
                ),
                key=lambda elem: elem.dt_created,
            )
            short_link = short_links[0] if short_links else None

        if short_link:
            return short_link
        return super().create(validated_data)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Execute raw SQL against a Grafana data source and print the result cleanly.

Usage:
  grafana-query.py "SELECT count(*) FROM my_table" [options]

Options:
  --ds NAME_OR_UID  data source name or uid (default: $GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS, else the
                    only data source visible to the token; with several visible
                    data sources the command refuses and lists candidates — never
                    guessing, a wrong DS queries another service's database;
                    pass a uid to skip the lookup)
  --var NAME=RAW    substitute $NAME with RAW in the SQL (raw substitution,
                    as Grafana interpolates the variable; repeatable)
  --from TIME       window start: "now-1d", "now-4h", ISO (default: now-1d)
  --to TIME         window end (default: now)
  --format FMT      time_series|table (default: table)
  --timeout SECS    request timeout (default: 60)

The SQL may reference ${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss} / ${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD
HH:mm:ss} — they are replaced from --from/--to.

Env overrides: GRAFANA_HOST, GRAFANA_TOKEN_FILE, GRAFANA_SCHEME, GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS
(see grafana_common).
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 query/API error, 2 usage or token error, 3 transport error.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import re
import sys
import time
from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone

import grafana_common as g

DEFAULT_DS_ENV = "GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS"  # fallback data source name/uid when --ds is absent


def list_datasources():
    """GET /api/datasources with one retry. List of DS dicts, or None when the
    listing itself is unavailable (do not guess uids then)."""
    for attempt in (1, 2):
        try:
            status, raw = g.request("GET", "datasources")
            if 200 <= status < 300:
                return json.loads(raw)
        except g.TransportError:
            pass
        if attempt == 2:
            return None
        time.sleep(1)
    return None


def resolve_ds(ds, sources):
    """Resolve a data source reference (uid or name) against a DS listing to
    (uid, type). Exact uid match wins; otherwise exact name match; otherwise
    pass the value through as a uid and let the API report the error.
    """
    by_uid = {s.get("uid"): s for s in sources}
    if ds in by_uid:
        return ds, by_uid[ds].get("type", "postgres")
    by_name = [s for s in sources if s.get("name") == ds]
    if by_name:
        if len(by_name) > 1:
            print(f"Warning: {len(by_name)} data sources named {ds!r}; using {by_name[0].get('uid')}",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        return by_name[0].get("uid"), by_name[0].get("type", "postgres")
    return ds, "postgres"


def resolve_time(spec: str) -> str:
    """Resolve a Grafana-style time spec ('now-1d', ISO) to 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' (UTC)."""
    m = re.fullmatch(r"now(?:-([0-9]+)([mhdwMy]))?", spec.strip())
    if m:
        n, unit = int(m.group(1) or 0), m.group(2) or "s"
        delta = {
            "s": timedelta(seconds=n), "m": timedelta(minutes=n), "h": timedelta(hours=n),
            "d": timedelta(days=n), "w": timedelta(weeks=n), "M": timedelta(days=30 * n),
            "y": timedelta(days=365 * n),
        }[unit]
        now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
        return (now - delta).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
    return spec.strip()


def main() -> int:
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument("sql")
    ap.add_argument("--ds", default=None,
                    help="data source name or uid (default: $%s, else the only "
                         "visible data source; see module docstring)" % DEFAULT_DS_ENV)
    ap.add_argument("--var", action="append", default=[], metavar="NAME=RAW")
    ap.add_argument("--from", dest="tfrom", default="now-1d")
    ap.add_argument("--to", dest="tto", default="now")
    ap.add_argument("--format", dest="fmt", default="table", choices=["time_series", "table"])
    ap.add_argument("--timeout", type=int, default=60)
    args = ap.parse_args()

    sql = args.sql
    sql = sql.replace("${__from:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}", resolve_time(args.tfrom))
    sql = sql.replace("${__to:date:YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm:ss}", resolve_time(args.tto))
    for item in args.var:
        if "=" not in item:
            print(f"Error: --var expects NAME=RAW, got {item!r}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 2
        name, raw = item.split("=", 1)
        sql = sql.replace(f"${name}", raw)

    sources = list_datasources()
    if sources is None:
        print(f"Error: cannot list data sources on {g.host()} — Grafana unreachable? "
              "Pass an explicit uid via --ds.", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    ds_ref = args.ds or os.environ.get(DEFAULT_DS_ENV)
    if not ds_ref:
        if len(sources) == 1:
            ds_ref = sources[0].get("name") or sources[0].get("uid")
            print(f"note: no --ds given; using the only visible data source: {ds_ref!r}",
                  file=sys.stderr)
        else:
            names = ", ".join(s.get("name") or s.get("uid") for s in sources)
            print(f"Error: no --ds given and the token can see {len(sources)} data "
                  f"sources ({names}). Pick one with --ds or set GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS — "
                  "refusing to guess (a wrong DS queries another service's database).",
                  file=sys.stderr)
            return 2

    ds_uid, ds_type = resolve_ds(ds_ref, sources)

    body = {
        "queries": [{
            "refId": "A",
            "datasource": {"type": ds_type, "uid": ds_uid},
            "rawSql": sql,
            "rawQuery": True,
            "format": args.fmt,
            "intervalMs": 3600000,
            "maxDataPoints": 330,
        }],
        "from": args.tfrom,
        "to": args.tto,
    }

    try:
        status, raw = g.request("POST", "ds/query", body=body, timeout=args.timeout)
    except g.TransportError as e:
        print(f"ERROR: transport: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 3
    if not 200 <= status < 300:
        print(f"ERROR: HTTP {status}: {raw[:300]}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    resp = json.loads(raw)

    result = resp.get("results", {}).get("A", {})
    if result.get("error"):
        print(f"ERROR: {result['error']}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    if not result.get("frames"):
        print("(no data)")
        return 0

    frame = result["frames"][0]
    fields = frame["schema"]["fields"]
    values = frame.get("data", {}).get("values", [])
    n_rows = frame.get("length") or (len(values[0]) if values else 0)

    print(f"# fields: " + ", ".join(f"{f['name']}({f['type']})" for f in fields))

    def fmt(i, v):
        if v is None:
            return "NULL"
        if fields[i]["type"] == "time":
            return datetime.fromtimestamp(v / 1000).strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
        if isinstance(v, float):
            return f"{v:,.2f}".rstrip("0").rstrip(".") if abs(v) < 1e15 else f"{v:,.0f}"
        return str(v)

    if n_rows == 1:
        for i, f in enumerate(fields):
            print(f"{f['name']}: {fmt(i, values[i][0]) if values[i] else 'NULL'}")
        return 0

    MAX_ROWS = 50
    cols = [[values[i][r] if i < len(values) and r < len(values[i]) else None for r in range(n_rows)]
            for i in range(len(fields))]
    widths = [max(len(f["name"]), *(len(fmt(i, c[r])) for r in range(n_rows))) if n_rows else len(f["name"])
              for i, f, c in ((i, fields[i], cols[i]) for i in range(len(fields)))]
    print("  ".join(f["name"].ljust(widths[i]) for i, f in enumerate(fields)))
    for r in range(min(n_rows, MAX_ROWS)):
        print("  ".join(fmt(i, cols[i][r]).ljust(widths[i]) for i, f in enumerate(fields)))
    if n_rows > MAX_ROWS:
        print(f"… ({n_rows - MAX_ROWS} more rows — narrow the window or aggregate)")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""grafana-dashboard.py — dashboard ops: get / import / duplicate / move / search.

Usage:
  grafana-dashboard.py get UID [--json]      (default: short summary)
  grafana-dashboard.py import FILE [--uid NEW_UID] [--title NEW_TITLE]
                         [--folder F] [--no-verify]
  grafana-dashboard.py duplicate SRC_UID --new-uid NEW_UID
                         [--title NEW_TITLE] [--folder F]
  grafana-dashboard.py move UID --folder F
  grafana-dashboard.py search QUERY

F = folder uid or title (case-insensitive); "root"/"general" = General folder.

Enforced behavior (code, not convention):
  * saves go through POST /api/dashboards/db — the canonical upstream endpoint
    (the platform's POST /dashboards/import is a non-upstream custom-build
    addition, used only as a last-resort re-save).
  * stale `id` is ALWAYS stripped from the dashboard JSON before saving
    (stale id + different uid => "Dashboard not found" in 11.1.3).
  * the target folder is ALWAYS pinned explicitly in the save command:
    --folder wins; otherwise an existing uid keeps its current folder
    (a save without folderId silently moves the dashboard to General);
    a new uid goes to General.
  * after every save the dashboard is READ BACK and verified. Fresh
    dashboards carry a stale permission verdict on the platform instance
    (measured: 403 up to ~55s after creation, readable by ~70s, and it
    clears on its own — NO re-save needed), so verification backs off
    0/15/40/65s before one last-resort re-save, then fails loudly.
  * import REFUSES A STALE BASE: when the file carries a `version` and the
    target uid exists, the versions must match — a copy fetched before
    someone else's save would silently roll back their panels (a save
    replaces the WHOLE dashboard). `--force` overrides the check.
  * duplicate's default title embeds the NEW uid: the slug is derived from
    the title, and a save whose slug already exists is SILENTLY redirected
    to the dashboard that owns the slug (the requested uid is dropped).

Output: one result line on stdout ("ok: ..." or the summary/JSON),
errors on stderr. Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 API error, 2 usage error, 3 transport.
Env overrides: GRAFANA_HOST, GRAFANA_TOKEN_FILE, GRAFANA_SCHEME.
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys
import time

import grafana_common as g

BACKOFF_DELAYS = (0, 15, 40, 65)  # seconds; cumulative 0/15/55/120


def usage_error(msg):
    print("Error: %s" % msg, file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


# ------------------------------------------------------------- pure logic

def build_save_payload(dash, folder_id):
    """Save payload for POST /api/dashboards/db with the folder pinned.

    The stale `id` is dropped: combined with a different uid it makes 11.1.3
    fail the save with "Dashboard not found".
    """
    dash = dict(dash)
    dash.pop("id", None)
    payload = {"dashboard": dash, "overwrite": True}
    if folder_id:
        payload["folderId"] = folder_id
    return payload


def resolve_folder_id(f, folders):
    """Folder uid or title (case-insensitive) -> id. ''/root/general -> 0."""
    if not f or f.lower() in ("root", "general"):
        return 0
    for x in folders:
        if x.get("uid") == f or x.get("title") == f:
            return x["id"]
    low = f.lower()
    for x in folders:
        if (x.get("title") or "").lower() == low:
            return x["id"]
    usage_error("no folder with uid or title %r" % f)


def load_dashboard_file(path, new_uid=None, new_title=None):
    try:
        with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
            dash = json.load(f)
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError) as e:
        usage_error("cannot read %s: %s" % (path, e))
    if not isinstance(dash, dict):
        usage_error("file must contain a single dashboard JSON object")
    if new_uid:
        dash["uid"] = new_uid
    if new_title:
        dash["title"] = new_title
    if not dash.get("uid"):
        usage_error("dashboard has no uid (pass --uid)")
    return dash


def current_version(uid):
    """Current version of an existing dashboard, or None when it does not
    exist / is unreadable."""
    try:
        status, raw = g.request("GET", "dashboards/uid/%s" % uid)
    except g.TransportError as e:
        print("Error: request failed (network/TLS/timeout): %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(3)
    if 200 <= status < 300:
        d = json.loads(raw)
        return d.get("meta", {}).get("version") or d["dashboard"].get("version")
    return None


def check_fresh_base(dash):
    """Refuse to overwrite an existing dashboard from a stale cached copy.

    A save replaces the WHOLE dashboard, so a file fetched before someone
    else's save would silently roll back their panels. Skipped when the file
    has no `version` (hand-written JSON) or the uid does not exist yet.
    """
    file_version = dash.get("version")
    if file_version is None:
        return
    server_version = current_version(dash["uid"])
    if server_version is None:
        return
    if str(file_version) != str(server_version):
        print("Error: %s is at version %s on the server, the file has %s — "
              "the file is a stale copy and this save would roll back edits "
              "made since it was fetched. Re-fetch it (get %s --json) or pass "
              "--force to overwrite anyway."
              % (dash["uid"], server_version, file_version, dash["uid"]),
              file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)


# --------------------------------------------------------- API wrappers

def get_folders():
    return json.loads(g.call("GET", "folders"))


def get_dashboard(uid):
    """Full GET response ({"dashboard": ..., "meta": ...}); exit 1 on error."""
    return json.loads(g.call("GET", "dashboards/uid/%s" % uid))


def current_folder_id(uid):
    """Folder id of an existing dashboard, or 0 (General) when unknown."""
    try:
        status, raw = g.request("GET", "dashboards/uid/%s" % uid)
    except g.TransportError as e:
        print("Error: request failed (network/TLS/timeout): %s" % e,
              file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(3)
    if 200 <= status < 300:
        return json.loads(raw).get("meta", {}).get("folderId") or 0
    return 0


def pin_folder(uid, folder_override=None):
    """Folder id to pin in the save command: explicit override wins, else the
    current folder of an existing uid, else General (0)."""
    if folder_override is not None:
        return resolve_folder_id(folder_override, get_folders())
    return current_folder_id(uid)


def save(dash, folder_id):
    payload = build_save_payload(dash, folder_id)
    resp = json.loads(g.call("POST", "dashboards/db", body=payload))
    return resp, payload


def readback_ok(uid):
    try:
        status, _ = g.request("GET", "dashboards/uid/%s" % uid)
    except g.TransportError:
        return False
    return 200 <= status < 300


def verify_with_backoff(uid, payload, delays=BACKOFF_DELAYS, sleep=time.sleep):
    """Read-back with TTL backoff (see module docstring). Exits 1 on failure."""
    for delay in delays:
        if delay:
            sleep(delay)
            print("permission verdict still stale; re-reading in %ds..." % delay,
                  file=sys.stderr)
        if readback_ok(uid):
            return
    print("still denied after backoff; last-resort re-save via "
          "POST /dashboards/import...", file=sys.stderr)
    healed = False
    for path in ("dashboards/import", "dashboards/db"):
        try:
            status, _ = g.request("POST", path, body=payload)
            healed = 200 <= status < 300
        except g.TransportError:
            pass
        if healed:
            break
    if healed:
        sleep(5)
        if readback_ok(uid):
            return
    print("Error: dashboard %s was saved but is unreadable after backoff + "
          "re-save. If a stale permission verdict is the cause it clears in "
          "~60s — retry the read, or re-save from the Grafana UI." % uid,
          file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def do_save(dash, folder_id, verify=True):
    resp, payload = save(dash, folder_id)
    uid = resp.get("uid")
    if not uid:
        print("Error: save response missing uid: %s" % resp, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    if verify:
        verify_with_backoff(uid, payload)
    print("ok: uid=%s version=%s folder='%s' %s" % (
        uid, resp.get("version", "?"),
        resp.get("folderUid") or "General", resp.get("url", "")))


# -------------------------------------------------------- subcommands

def cmd_get(args):
    r = get_dashboard(args.uid)
    if args.json:
        print(json.dumps(r, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2))
        return 0
    d, m = r["dashboard"], r.get("meta", {})
    refs = sorted({json.dumps(t.get("datasource"))
                   for p in d.get("panels", []) for t in p.get("targets", [])})
    print("title:    %s" % d.get("title"))
    print("uid:      %s" % d.get("uid"))
    print("version:  %s" % (m.get("version") or d.get("version")))
    print("folder:   %s (uid=%r, id=%s)" % (
        m.get("folderTitle") or "General", m.get("folderUid"), m.get("folderId")))
    print("panels:   %d" % len(d.get("panels", [])))
    print("time:     %s" % d.get("time"))
    print("ds refs:  %s" % refs)
    for v in d.get("templating", {}).get("list", []):
        print("var %s: ds=%s allValue=%r" % (
            v["name"], json.dumps(v.get("datasource")), v.get("allValue")))
    return 0


def cmd_import(args):
    # The file's ORIGINAL uid (before any --uid override): the version check
    # only applies when saving under the file's own uid — with a different
    # --uid the file's `version` refers to the SOURCE dashboard, not the
    # target (clone-style import).
    with open(args.file, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        file_uid = json.load(f).get("uid")
    dash = load_dashboard_file(args.file, args.uid, args.title)
    if not args.force and args.uid in (None, file_uid):
        check_fresh_base(dash)
    folder_id = pin_folder(dash["uid"], args.folder)
    do_save(dash, folder_id, verify=not args.no_verify)
    return 0


def cmd_duplicate(args):
    src = get_dashboard(args.src)["dashboard"]
    # Default title embeds the NEW uid: the slug derives from the title, and a
    # save whose slug already exists is silently redirected to the dashboard
    # that owns the slug (the requested uid is dropped) — measured on 11.1.3.
    title = args.title or ("%s (%s)" % (src.get("title", ""), args.new_uid))
    dash = dict(src)
    dash["uid"] = args.new_uid
    dash["title"] = title
    folder_id = pin_folder(args.new_uid, args.folder)
    do_save(dash, folder_id, verify=True)
    return 0


def cmd_move(args):
    dash = get_dashboard(args.uid)["dashboard"]
    folder_id = resolve_folder_id(args.folder, get_folders())
    do_save(dash, folder_id, verify=True)
    return 0


def cmd_search(args):
    raw = g.call("GET", "search", params={"query": args.query})
    for d in json.loads(raw):
        print("%-28s v%-4s %-20s %s" % (
            d.get("uid", "-"), d.get("version", "-"),
            d.get("folderTitle") or "General", d.get("title", "")))
    return 0


def main(argv=None):
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="grafana-dashboard.py",
        description="Grafana dashboard ops (get / import / duplicate / move / search).")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", metavar="COMMAND")

    p = sub.add_parser("get", help="overview (default) or full JSON of a dashboard")
    p.add_argument("uid")
    p.add_argument("--json", action="store_true", help="full JSON instead of summary")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_get)

    p = sub.add_parser("import", help="create/overwrite a dashboard from a JSON file")
    p.add_argument("file")
    p.add_argument("--uid", help="override the uid from the file")
    p.add_argument("--title", help="override the title from the file")
    p.add_argument("--folder", help="target folder uid/title ('root' = General); "
                                    "default: keep the current folder")
    p.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
                   help="import even if the file's version is stale relative "
                        "to the server (see the stale-base check)")
    p.add_argument("--no-verify", action="store_true",
                   help="skip the read-back verification")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_import)

    p = sub.add_parser("duplicate", help="clone a dashboard under a new uid")
    p.add_argument("src")
    p.add_argument("--new-uid", required=True)
    p.add_argument("--title",
                   help="default: '<src title> (<new-uid>)' — the slug must not "
                        "collide with an existing dashboard's slug")
    p.add_argument("--folder", help="target folder uid/title ('root' = General)")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_duplicate)

    p = sub.add_parser("move", help="move a dashboard to a folder")
    p.add_argument("uid")
    p.add_argument("--folder", required=True,
                   help="folder uid or title ('root' = General)")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_move)

    p = sub.add_parser("search", help="list dashboards (matches title/tags — NOT uid)")
    p.add_argument("query")
    p.set_defaults(fn=cmd_search)

    args = ap.parse_args(argv)
    if not getattr(args, "fn", None):
        ap.print_help(sys.stderr)
        return 2
    return args.fn(args)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def run_query(ds_type, ds_uid, sql, tfrom="now-24h", tto="now", fmt="table", timeout=60):
    """POST /api/ds/query with the per-type body shape (see verified.json).
    Returns (frame: dict|None, error: str|None). frame = results.A.frames[0]."""
    body = {
        "queries": [build_query_body(ds_type, ds_uid, sql, fmt)],
        "from": tfrom, "to": tto,
    }
    try:
        status, raw = request("POST", "ds/query", body=body, timeout=timeout)
    except TransportError as e:
        return None, "transport: %s" % e
    if not 200 <= status < 300:
        return None, "HTTP %d: %s" % (status, raw[:300])
    res = json.loads(raw).get("results", {}).get("A", {})
    if res.get("error"):
        return None, res["error"]
    frames = res.get("frames") or []
    return (frames[0] if frames else None), None
```
Note: g.request (not g.call) — no exit, return a tuple. grafana-query keeps its own output handling.

arguments.content:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""grafana-ds.py — data source discovery: which DB is where, what it holds.

Usage:
  grafana-ds.py list                        all visible data sources + probed
                                             current database (PG) / databases (CH)
  grafana-ds.py tables NAME_OR_UID          tables of the DS's current database
  grafana-ds.py find-table TABLE_NAME       which data sources contain this table
  grafana-ds.py functions NAME_OR_UID --check a,b,c
                                             (ClickHouse) check function availability
                                             via system.functions

Answers the questions that otherwise cost a loop of ad-hoc probes:
  * "is MY service's database even registered as a data source?" -> list
  * "which DS does table X live in?"                            -> find-table
  * "does this ClickHouse build have function Y?"               -> functions
Supported types: grafana-postgresql-datasource / postgres / grafana-clickhouse-datasource.
Other types are listed but not probed (no assumptions about their schema).

Output contract as the other helpers (body on stdout, "HTTP ..." lines and
errors on stderr). Exit: 0 ok, 1 API/query error, 2 usage, 3 transport.
Env overrides: GRAFANA_HOST, GRAFANA_TOKEN_FILE, GRAFANA_SCHEME (grafana_common).
"""
import argparse
import json
import sys

import grafana_common as g

PG_TYPES = ("grafana-postgresql-datasource", "postgres")
CH_TYPES = ("grafana-clickhouse-datasource",)


def list_sources():
    try:
        status, raw = g.request("GET", "datasources")
    except g.TransportError as e:
        print("Error: %s" % e, file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(3)
    if not 200 <= status < 300:
        print("Error: HTTP %d listing data sources: %s" % (status, raw[:200]),
              file=sys.stderr)
        sys.exit(1)
    return json.loads(raw)


def resolve(ds_ref, sources):
    for s in sources:
        if s.get("uid") == ds_ref or s.get("name") == ds_ref:
            return s
    print("Error: no data source with uid or name %r (see: list)" % ds_ref,
          file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(2)


def probe_current(sources, s, timeout=30):
    """Human-readable 'where does this DS point' for PG/CH, else '-'."""
    t, u = s.get("type"), s.get("uid")
    if t in PG_TYPES:
        frame, err = g.run_query(t, u, "SELECT current_database() d, current_user u",
                                 timeout=timeout)
        if err or not frame:
            return "- (%s)" % (err or "no frame")[:60]
        v = frame["data"]["values"]
        return "%s@%s" % (v[0][0], v[1][0]) if v[0] and v[1] else "-"
    if t in CH_TYPES:
        frame, err = g.run_query(t, u, "SHOW DATABASES", timeout=timeout)
        if err or not frame:
            return "- (%s)" % (err or "no frame")[:60]
        return ",".join(frame["data"]["values"][0])
    return "-"


def list_tables(s, timeout=30):
    """(tables:list[str], error:str|None) for the DS's current database."""
    t, u = s.get("type"), s.get("uid")
    if t in PG_TYPES:
        sql = ("SELECT tablename FROM pg_tables WHERE schemaname='public' "
               "ORDER BY tablename")
    elif t in CH_TYPES:
        sql = "SHOW TABLES"
    else:
        return None, "unsupported type %r" % t
    frame, err = g.run_query(t, u, sql, timeout=timeout)
    if err:
        return None, err
    if not frame:
        return [], None
    return [r[0] for r in zip(*frame["data"]["values"])] if frame["data"]["values"] else [], None


def cmd_list(_args):
    sources = list_sources()
    rows = []
    for s in sorted(sources, key=lambda x: (x.get("type") or "", x.get("name") or "")):
        rows.append((s.get("uid") or "-", s.get("name") or "-", s.get("type") or "-",
                     s.get("url") or "-", probe_current(sources, s)))
    w = [max(len(h), *(len(r[i]) for r in rows)) if rows else len(h)
         for i, h in enumerate(("uid", "name", "type", "url", "current db"))]
    print("  ".join(h.ljust(w[i]) for i, h in enumerate(("uid", "name", "type", "url", "current db"))))
    for r in rows:
        print("  ".join(str(x).ljust(w[i]) for i, x in enumerate(r)))
    print("# %d data sources visible to the token" % len(rows), file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


def cmd_tables(args):
    sources = list_sources()
    s = resolve(args.ds, sources)
    tables, err = list_tables(s)
    if err:
        print("Error: %s" % err, file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    for t in tables:
        print(t)
    print("# %d tables in %s (%s)" % (len(tables), s.get("name"), s.get("uid")),
          file=sys.stderr)
    return 0


def cmd_find_table(args):
    sources = list_sources()
    found = []
    for s in sources:
        tables, err = list_tables(s)
        if err:
            print("note: %s (%s): not probed: %s" % (s.get("name"), s.get("uid"), err),
                  file=sys.stderr)
            continue
        if args.table in tables:
            found.append(s)
    if not found:
        print("not found: table %r is in NONE of the %d visible data sources — "
              "it either does not exist or its database is not registered "
              "(a new data source must be created before it can be charted)"
              % (args.table, len(sources)))
        return 1
    for s in found:
        print("%-24s %s  (uid=%s, type=%s)" % (s.get("name"), s.get("url"),
                                               s.get("uid"), s.get("type")))
    return 0


def cmd_functions(args):
    sources = list_sources()
    s = resolve(args.ds, sources)
    if s.get("type") not in CH_TYPES:
        print("Error: functions check is ClickHouse-only (this DS is %r)"
              % s.get("type"), file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    names = [x.strip() for x in args.check.split(",") if x.strip()]
    if not names:
        print("Error: --check needs a comma-separated function list", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    in_list = ", ".join("'%s'" % n.replace("'", "") for n in names)
    frame, err = g.run_query(s.get("type"), s.get("uid"),
                             "SELECT name FROM system.functions WHERE name IN (%s)" % in_list)
    if err:
        print("Error: %s" % err, file=sys.stderr)

def _substitute(sql, var_modes, from_iso, to_iso):
    """Grafana-style interpolation for validation purposes:
    - $__timeFilter(col) -> (col >= 'from' AND col <= 'to')
    - ${__from:date:...} / ${__to:date:...} -> resolved ISO
    - $name -> the per-mode substitution value (variable)
    """
    sql = re.sub(r"\$__timeFilter\(([^)]+)\)",
                 r"(\1 >= '%s' AND \1 <= '%s')" % (from_iso, to_iso), sql)
    sql = re.sub(r"\$\{__from:date[^}]*\}", from_iso, sql)
    sql = re.sub(r"\$\{__to:date[^}]*\}", to_iso, sql)
    for name, val in var_modes:  # longest name first (avoid partial replacements)
        sql = sql.replace("$%s" % name, val)
    return sql
```

def _var_modes(dash, tfrom, tto, timeout):
    """name -> list of (label, substitution value) — including the All mode when includeAll.
    Substitution rule is per DS type (see verified.json):
      classic PG: option values quoted, allValue as-is
      ClickHouse: everything as-is (option values need to carry quotes themselves)
    Returns (modes, errors) — errors: variable queries that couldn't be executed."""
    modes, errors = {}, []
    for v in dash.get("templating", {}).get("list", []):
        if v.get("type") != "query" or not v.get("query"):
            continue
        ds = v.get("datasource") or {}
        ds_uid = ds.get("uid")
        ds_type = ds.get("type") or "grafana-postgresql-datasource"
        frame, err = g.run_query(ds_type, ds_uid, v["query"], tfrom=tfrom, tto=tto, timeout=timeout)
        if err:
            errors.append("variable %r: %s" % (v["name"], err))
            continue
        opts = []
        if frame and frame["data"]["values"]:
            opts = [str(x) for x in frame["data"]["values"][0]]
        modes_list = []
        if v.get("includeAll"):
            modes_list.append(("All", v.get("allValue") or "'All'"))
        for o in opts:
            if g.is_clickhouse(ds_type):
                modes_list.append((o, o))  # raw substitution — option carries its own quotes
            else:
                modes_list.append((o, "'%s'" % o.replace("'", "''")))  # PG plugin quotes option values
        if modes_list:
            modes[v["name"]] = modes_list
    return modes, errors

---
name: grafana-api
description: Use when you need to make Grafana REST API calls (dashboards, data sources, ad-hoc SQL against the platform PostgreSQL, alerting endpoints) or work with Grafana dashboards stored in a repo's grafana/ folder — import, verify queries, read back state.
---

# Grafana REST API

Direct Grafana API access for the platform instance (`grafana-platform.medrocket.ru`,
Grafana **11.1.3** — a *custom build*: health reports commit `da5a557b…`, a couple of
endpoints/quirks differ from upstream, see below), classic PostgreSQL (and other)
data sources; other instances via env overrides. The skill is service-agnostic:
the token sees EVERY service's data sources — always pin yours (see Quick Reference).

## Quick Reference

- **Token:** `~/.tokens/grafana-platform.medrocket.ru/token.txt` (service-account `glsa_...`)
- **Base URL:** `https://grafana-platform.medrocket.ru/api`
- **Auth Header:** `Authorization: Bearer <token>`
- **API Docs:** `https://grafana.com/docs/grafana/latest/developers/http_api/`
- **Raw helper:** `~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana.py`
- **SQL query:** `~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-query.py`
- **Dashboards:** `~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py`
- **Alerts:** `~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py`
- **Shared HTTP layer:** `scripts/grafana_common.py` (token/host/env, one client, the contract)
- **Data sources:** one per service on the platform instance (the DS name is the
  service name). Name ≠ uid (see gotchas) — resolve via `GET /api/datasources` and
  pin yours with `--ds` (or `GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS` for `grafana-query.py`).

All helpers are **Python, stdlib only** (urllib — no curl, no jq dependency),
share `grafana_common.py`, and share one output contract (below).

Other instances / defaults: `GRAFANA_HOST=<host> GRAFANA_SCHEME=http GRAFANA_TOKEN_FILE=<file>`
select a different host + token (the host also names the default token dir);
`GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS=<name-or-uid>` sets the default data source for `grafana-query.py`.

## Helper Scripts

### `grafana.py` — raw API call

```bash
# GET
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana.py GET "health"
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana.py GET "datasources" | jq -r '.[].uid + " " + .[].name'

# POST / PUT with JSON body
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana.py POST "dashboards/db" '{"dashboard":{...},"overwrite":true}'
```

Args: `METHOD PATH [query_string_or_json_body]` (query string for GET — appended
**verbatim**, you own the URL encoding; JSON body otherwise, also sent verbatim).

**Output contract (shared by ALL helper scripts):**

- `stdout` — the response body **only** (empty on 204). Pipe straight into `jq`,
  nothing to strip.
- `stderr` — one line per call: `HTTP <status> <METHOD> /api/<path>`.
- Exit codes: `0` = 2xx · `1` = other HTTP status (body still on stdout) ·
  `2` = usage/token · `3` = transport (DNS/TLS/timeout).

### `grafana-query.py` — run SQL, get a clean table

The workhorse for "what does this data look like / does this query work". Stdlib-only,
sends the SQL through the Grafana data source, substitutes `${__from...}`/`${__to...}`
and `$variable` occurrences, and prints columns (scalar queries → `name: value` lines).

```bash
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-query.py \
  "SELECT count(*) FROM my_table WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '24 hours'"

# window + variables (raw substitution — see variable-quoting gotcha)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-query.py \
  "SELECT count(*) FROM my_table WHERE kind = 'direct'" \
  --from now-7d --to now

# pick a data source (name or uid — names are resolved via GET /api/datasources)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-query.py "SELECT 1" --ds my_service
```

Defaults: `--ds` = `$GRAFANA_DEFAULT_DS` env, else the ONLY data source visible to
the token (with several visible the command refuses and lists candidates — never
guessing: a wrong DS means silently querying another service's database). Name or
uid (uid skips the lookup; the DS `type` is taken from the listing, so non-PostgreSQL
sources work too). Window `now-1d`..`now`, `--format table`.
Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` query/API error, `2` usage/token, `3` transport.

### `grafana-alerts.py` — alert rules (provisioning API, provenance header baked in)

`apply` dry-runs the rule's SQL via `/api/ds/query` **before** committing (catches syntax
errors without touching the rule). Updates and pause/unpause go through the **group PUT**
(`.../folder/{folderUid}/rule-groups/{group}`); fallback is delete+recreate.

```bash
# list all / by group / by folder  (uid | paused | group | title)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py list [--group my-group]

# full rule JSON — template for manual edits
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py show <uid>

# pause/unpause one or more (group PUT; recreate fallback)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py pause <uid>...
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py unpause <uid>...

# upsert a rule file (provisioning shape with "uid"): SQL dry-run, then group PUT if
# exists / collection POST if new
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py apply rule.json

# delete; --clean-group also removes the ruler group if it becomes empty
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-alerts.py delete <uid> --clean-group
```

Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` API error, `2` usage, `3` transport.

### `grafana-dashboard.py` — get / import / duplicate / move / search

```bash
# compact overview: title, version, folder, panel count, all data-source refs, variables + allValue
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py get <uid>

# full JSON
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py get <uid> --json

# import (create/overwrite; --folder defaults to the CURRENT folder of the uid;
# refuses a stale file `version` — see gotchas — unless --force)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py import grafana/<name>.json \
  [--uid U] [--title T] [--folder F] [--force] [--no-verify]

# clone under a new uid (default title: "<src title> (<new-uid>)" — slug-safe)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py duplicate <uid> --new-uid clone-2

# move to a folder (uid or title, case-insensitive; root/general = General)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py move <uid> --folder <folder>

# search (matches title/tags — NOT uid; case-sensitive)
~/.pi/agent/skills/grafana-api/scripts/grafana-dashboard.py search "some title word"
```

Behavior **enforced in code, not by convention** (each one cost real pain):

- Saves go through `POST /api/dashboards/db` (canonical upstream endpoint). The
  platform's `POST /api/dashboards/import` is a **non-upstream custom-build**
  addition; the script only falls back to it as a last-resort re-save.
- A stale `id` in the dashboard JSON is **always stripped** before saving
  (stale id + different uid ⇒ "Dashboard not found" on 11.1.3).
- `import` **refuses a stale base**: a file carrying a `version` for an existing
  uid must match the server's current version, or the save is declined and
  nothing is written (a save replaces the WHOLE dashboard, so a cached copy
  fetched before someone else's save would silently roll back their panels).
  `--force` overrides; the check is skipped for new uids and for `--uid`
  clone-style imports (there the file's version refers to the source).
- The target folder is **always pinned** in the save command: `--folder` wins,
  otherwise an existing uid keeps its current folder. A save without `folderId`
  silently moves the dashboard to General (see gotchas) — "just update the JSON"
  is never folder-neutral.
- Every save is **read-back-verified with backoff**: fresh dashboards carry a
  stale permission verdict (measured: 403 up to ~55s, readable by ~120s, clears
  on its own — no re-save needed). Delays 0/15/40/65s, then one last-resort
  re-save, then a loud failure with what to do. `--no-verify` skips this.
- `duplicate`'s default title embeds the **new** uid: the slug derives from the
  title, and a save whose slug already exists is **silently redirected** to the
  dashboard that owns the slug (see gotchas).

Exit codes: `0` ok, `1` API error, `2` usage, `3` transport.

## Verified endpoints

- `GET /api/health` — version + db status (start here to check the token).
- `GET /api/dashboards/uid/{uid}` — one dashboard (`{"dashboard", "meta", "uri"}`).
- **`POST /api/dashboards/db`** — the canonical SAVE (create/update/move): body
  `{"dashboard": {...}, "overwrite": true, "folderId": <id>}`; import bumps
  `version`. There is **no** `POST /dashboards/uid/{uid}` save route in 11.1.3.
  `folderId` is what actually moves a dashboard (0 = General); see the folderId
  gotcha before omitting it.
- `POST /api/dashboards/import` — **platform custom-build only** (NOT in upstream
  11.1.3 — this instance is a patched build); behaves like `/db`. The helpers
  use `/db` and only fall back to this as a last-resort re-save.
- `GET /api/search?query=...` (NOT `/api/dashboards/search` — that 404s)
- `GET /api/folders` — folder id/uid/title mapping (folders are usually per-service).
- `GET /api/datasources` — **only the data sources the token can see**; each has
  `id`, `uid`, `type`, `name`, `url`.
- `POST /api/ds/query` — ad-hoc query (see `grafana-query.py`); body
  `{"queries":[{"refId","datasource":{"type","uid"},"rawSql","rawQuery":true,"format",
  "intervalMs","maxDataPoints"}], "from":"now-1d","to":"now"}`.
- **Alerting on the platform instance runs on an external Cortex/Mimir ruler.**
  **The SA token has FULL CRUD via the provisioning API** (this is the write path —
  the ruler proxy itself refuses SA writes):
  - `GET /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules` — list all rules (200)
  - `GET /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/{uid}` — one rule (200)
  - **`POST /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules`** — CREATE (201). `PUT` with a NEW uid
    404s — create goes through the collection POST.
  - **Group PUT is the reliable UPDATE path:**
    `GET/PUT /api/v1/provisioning/folder/{folderUid}/rule-groups/{groupTitle}` — body
    `{"title", "folderUid", "interval": <SECONDS>, "rules": [full rule objects]}`.
    Replaces the whole group: fetch → mutate one rule → PUT. Honors
    `X-Disable-Provenance`. Use it for updates AND pause/unpause toggles.
  - **`PUT /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/{uid}`** — single-rule update; **BROKEN on
    the platform instance** (500 even on fresh verbatim bodies; devops saw
    `error="cannot find rule in the delta"` in Grafana logs — a server-side delta-sync
    bug, not a payload issue). It worked early in one session and then regressed; don't
    depend on it.
  - `DELETE /api/v1/provisioning/alert-rules/{uid}` — 204. **Leaves the (empty) ruler
    group behind** — remove it via the ruler DELETE below.
  - **Always send `X-Disable-Provenance: true` on provisioning writes.** Without it the
    rule gets `"provenance": "api"` and becomes **uneditable from the UI** (Grafana treats
    it as externally managed).
  - **Un-stamping an existing `provenance` is impossible via PUT (500)** — DELETE + POST
    the same rule back (same `uid`, no `id`) instead. (isPaused toggling has the same
    symptom on the single-PUT path, but works fine via the group PUT above.)
  - Provisioning shape is **camelCase**: `isPaused`, `noDataState`, `execErrState`, plus
    `orgID`, `folderUID` (namespace uid), `ruleGroup`, `notification_settings`, `record`.
    Best template: GET a real rule, mutate, PUT back. No `id` on create.
  - Ruler proxy (`/api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/...?subtype=cortex`) with the SA token:
    read (all groups / by folder / one group) and `DELETE .../{nsUid}/{group}` (202) only;
    `POST`/`PUT` there 404 for SA (a user-session cookie can POST a whole group — see
    write shape below). Use it for group-level listing, `interval`, and cleanup.
  - **No runtime alert-state API** (firing/pending/ok, history) — definitions only;
    state is UI-only or inside Cortex.
  - `GET /api/folders` for namespace uids (folders are usually per-service).
  - Ruler group reads: `GET .../api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/rules?subtype=cortex` — ALL groups
    (response is a dict: `{namespaceUID: [groups...]}`)
    - `GET .../api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/rules/{nsUid}?subtype=cortex` — groups in a folder
    (202)
  - `GET .../api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/rules/{nsUid}/{groupName}?subtype=cortex` — one group
  - `DELETE .../api/ruler/grafana/api/v1/rules/{nsUid}/{groupName}?subtype=cortex` — 202

### Alert-rule write shapes — there are TWO, don't mix them!

**Provisioning API** (SA token, preferred): camelCase flat object
(`isPaused`/`noDataState`/`execErrState`, `orgID`, `folderUID`, `ruleGroup`, `title`,
`condition`, `for`, `labels`, `annotations`, `notification_settings`, `record`, `data`).

**Ruler POST body** (user-session cookie only — whole group in one request), captured
from the browser; the group `name` goes in the BODY (no group in the path; PUT/POST with
a group in the path 404):

```json
{"name": "<group>", "interval": "5m", "rules": [{
  "for": "0s",                          // rule-level, NOT inside grafana_alert
  "annotations": {"summary": "... {{ $values.C.Value }} ..."},   // rule-level
  "labels": {...},                       // rule-level
  "grafana_alert": {
    "title": "...", "condition": "C",
    "no_data_state": "NoData",           // snake_case!
    "exec_err_state": "Error",           // snake_case; platform convention: "Error"
    "is_paused": true,                   // snake_case; omit uid on create
    "data": [ <A query>, <B reduce last over A>, <C threshold over B> ]
  }
}]}
```

The proven chain: A = PG query (`datasourceUid` = real uid, `model` with `rawSql`),
B = `type: "reduce"`, `expression: "A"`, `reducer: "last"`, C = `type: "threshold"` with
`conditions: [{evaluator: {params: [0], type: "gt"}, ...}]`, `datasourceUid: "__expr__"`.
A simpler `condition: "A"` (threshold in the query itself) also exists in the fleet.
Reference group to copy from: any existing `it-platform*` group
(`grafana-alerts.py list`); new-service groups should follow the same naming.

## Gotchas (learned the hard way)

- **Data source uid ≠ name** (on the platform instance the DS name is the service
  name, and the uid is an unrelated random string). Dashboards/panels reference the
  **uid**; a wrong one gives
  `"Data source not found"` on every panel while the dashboard JSON looks fine.
  When porting a dashboard between Grafana instances, diff the uid first.
- **`/api/ds/query` frames are column-oriented:** `frame.data.values[i]` is the list of
  values for field `i` (not rows). Single-row queries: `values[i][0]`.
- **PG variable interpolation:** option values from a variable query are substituted
  **quoted** (`$var` → `'option-value'`), but the variable's **allValue is substituted
  raw**. The working pattern: unquoted `$var` in SQL
  (`AND ($var = 'All' OR column = $var)`) + a **quoted** allValue
  (`"allValue": "'All'"`). Both quoting it yourself *and* an unquoted allValue break:
  `''option-value''` (syntax error) or `All = 'All'` (bare identifier).
- **Alert rule queries cannot use dashboard variables** and have no dashboard time
  range — write self-contained SQL with `now() - interval '...'`.
- **Time columns:** in `time_series` format the classic PG source converts a `timestamptz`
  column to a time field; in `table` format that conversion is version-dependent
  (12.4.3 converts, 11.1.3 hands back epoch-ms numbers → `1.79 Tri` on the axis).
  Environment-proof pattern for a matrix pivot on time: query
  `EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM date_trunc('hour', created_at)) * 1000 AS "time"` (plain number)
  + transforms `groupingToMatrix` (row=time, column=<series>, value=<metric>) then
  `convertFieldType` on the pivot's time column
  (`"options":{"conversions":[{"targetField":"time\\<columnField>","destinationType":"time"}]}`
  — numeric input is read as epoch **milliseconds**).
- **Duration axis units (11.1.3):** the hh:mm:ss duration unit is **`dthms`**
  ("duration (hh:mm:ss)", Time category; zero-padded, hours unbounded, input in
  seconds). There is NO `hms` id — an unknown unit id renders as `NNN hms`
  (raw value + id). Siblings: `dtdurations` (s), `dtdurationms` (ms),
  `dtdhms` (d hh:mm:ss). Registry: `packages/grafana-data/src/valueFormats/categories.ts`.
- **The PG source has no "series column"** option (that's the MySQL source).
  Per-category series come from the matrix transform above.
- **Bar chart label crowding:** option `xTickLabelSpacing`
  (UI: "X-axis labels minimum spacing"; None=0 / Small=100 / Medium=200 / Large=300)
  in each barchart panel's `options` — time ticks on hourly buckets overlap without it.
- **Barchart's time X-axis is DATA-DRIVEN** (min/max of the returned rows), while
  **timeseries' time axis spans the panel's time range**. Same data, different
  axis width: a barchart whose data starts late fills the whole panel and looks
  like it shows "more data" than the timeseries next to it. Barchart has no
  time-axis min/max option. To pin a barchart's axis to the dashboard's time
  filter, return EVERY hour of the filter range from SQL: `generate_series(
  date_trunc('hour', $__from), date_trunc('hour', $__to), interval '1 hour')`
  LEFT JOINed to the aggregation, values `COALESCE(x, 0)`.
- **Importing a dashboard JSON with a STALE `id` + a DIFFERENT `uid` fails** with
  `"Dashboard not found"` (the pre-save validation chases the id). When cloning a
  dashboard under a new uid, drop `id` from the JSON first —
  `grafana-dashboard.py import/duplicate` do this automatically. (Same uid + same
  id is fine — that's a normal overwrite.)
- **Freshly created dashboards 403 on read for a while — a STALE PERMISSION
  VERDICT**, measured on the platform instance: 403 up to ~55s after create,
  readable by ~70–120s, and it clears **on its own, with no write**. Don't
  "fix" it by re-saving (bumps `version` for nothing, and the re-save can
  itself be 403'd) — back off and re-read. `grafana-dashboard.py` does exactly
  this (delays 0/15/40/65s, then a last-resort re-save via
  `/dashboards/import`, then a loud failure).
- **A save without `folderId` in the command relocates the dashboard to
  General.** `GetDashboardModel` overwrites the stored `folderId` with the
  command's value unconditionally (11.1.3, `pkg/services/dashboards/models.go`) —
  "update the JSON" is not folder-neutral. `grafana-dashboard.py` always pins
  the folder explicitly.
- **Slug collision = silent redirect.** The slug derives from the title. Saving
  a NEW uid whose slug already exists is silently redirected to the dashboard
  that OWNS the slug: the response's `uid` is the other dashboard's and the
  requested uid is never created (measured). Pick titles whose slug is free —
  the `duplicate` default `<src title> (<new-uid>)` is deterministic and unique.
- **`/api/search?query=` matches title and tags only — NOT uid — and is
  case-sensitive** (a Russian title needs the real case; URL-encode the
  query). To look a dashboard up by uid, use `GET /dashboards/uid/{uid}` or
  `grafana-dashboard.py get`.
- **`POST /rules/{ns}` and `PUT .../groups` replace the WHOLE group** — own the whole
  object, don't assume merge. (The `/api/v1/policies` full-tree-replace caveat applies
  where the standard API exists.)
- **Read vs write shape mismatch on the ruler:** reads give camelCase
  (`noDataState`, `isPaused`) + `expr`/`id`/`orgId`; writes want snake_case
  (`no_data_state`, `is_paused`), rule-level `for`/`annotations`/`labels`, and no `expr`.
  Copy a real group from the UI capture, not from the read API.
- **`count(*)` + `percentile_cont`:** `percentile_cont` over an empty set returns NULL
  (row still exists) — alert rules want `noDataState: NoData` to stay quiet when there
  is simply no traffic.

## Error Handling

- **401/403:** token missing/insufficient scope — check the file exists; the platform
  token is a service-account token with org-level access.
- **404 on `/api/datasources/uid/{uid}`:** the data source exists but is outside the
  token's view, or the uid is wrong — list `GET /api/datasources` and match by name.
- **`"Data source not found"` from `/api/ds/query`:** wrong uid in the query body.
- **`"Bad request"` / SQL errors from `/api/ds/query`:** the error text is in
  `results.A.error` — read it, don't guess.
